summary: Iter-14 — frontend-only E2E of all 4 P0 parity items (A Services, B Register, C AdminProducts, D AdminSystemWallet) against the real backend at https://network-pay-1.emergent.host. Tasks A, C, D PASS in full. Task B PASSES the happy path end-to-end (register .com email → reg-pay-step shows ₹100 + ₹18 GST = ₹118 → reg-pay-now POSTs /api/payment/register-fee 200 → routes to /dashboard). One real Register frontend bug found: when /api/auth/register returns 422 (Pydantic validation, detail=array), the page does not surface a reg-error and emits a React render warning (likely tries to render detail array as a string).

minor.issue: Returns 422 detail with FastAPI/Pydantic array format for .test TLD (IANA reserved). The test spec asked us to use email like web_test_{ts}@slangcart.test which the backend (correctly) rejects. Not a backend bug per se, but the spec example must use a real TLD such as .com or .in.

ui_bugs.issue: When /api/auth/register returns 422 with detail as an array of Pydantic errors, reg-error is NOT rendered. Console shows a React render warning ('An error occurred in the <div> component'), suggesting the catch block tries to render the array detail object directly. 400 with detail='Email already registered' (string) is handled correctly and surfaces in reg-error.

Empty-form submit relies on HTML5 native required attribute only (3 inputs have required); no custom reg-error message is rendered. The spec wording ('Empty/duplicate-email submission must show an error in reg-error') is only met for the duplicate-email branch.

issues: Spec stated testids g-group_2_operations / _3_partners / _4_wallets / _5_escrow / _6_payouts / _7_adjustments. Actual implementation uses g-group_2_liability, _3_gst, _4_platform_fee, _5_expenses, _6_pending_withdrawals, _7_bank. Pattern (g-group_{N}_{key}, all are <button>s, cursor:pointer, click → g-txns-modal with g-txns-table) is fully correct and working — only the key suffix names differ. Either update the spec/QA fixtures, or align the implementation. All 8 cards click into a working transactions modal.

action_items: Register.jsx — defensively coerce error to string before rendering. Suggested: const msg = typeof detail==='string' ? detail : Array.isArray(detail) ? detail.map(d=>d.msg||JSON.stringify(d)).join('; ') : (detail?.msg || JSON.stringify(detail||{})); setError(msg). This will make the 422 (array detail) path surface reg-error and stop the React render warning.

Register.jsx (optional) — add an early client-side guard before POST: if any of name/email/phone/password is empty, set reg-error to a friendly message instead of letting HTML5 silently block. Removes ambiguity for empty-submit assertion.

Update the agent-to-agent test prompt: registration emails must use a real TLD (.com / .in / .co); .test is reserved (IANA RFC 2606) and Pydantic EmailStr correctly rejects it. The fact that the test domain failed is what surfaced the 422-handling bug.

AdminSystemWallet — reconcile testid naming with the spec (rename to g-group_2_liability stays as-is in code if that is the intended canonical name; just correct the QA spec). Or rename in JSX to match the spec keywords. Pick one source of truth.
critical_code_review_comments: Services.jsx — categories + filter + ProviderProfileModal + reveal-fee + insufficient-funds gating ALL work as specified. Pay button correctly stays disabled (a) before checking svc-reveal-terms, AND (b) when wallet balance < total, with the red 'Wallet balance is insufficient' warning visible. svc-pay button text includes the total amount ('Pay ₹1.18 & reveal contact'). svc-profile-book and svc-profile-close work.

Register.jsx — happy path is correct: registration_paid falsy → reg-pay-step UI renders with full breakdown (₹100 fee, ₹18 GST, ₹118 total) → reg-pay-now button → POST /api/payment/register-fee 200 with approval_status='pending' → routes to /dashboard. Defensive error handling for 422-array is the only gap.

AdminProducts.jsx — ALL 25 expected ap-* data-testids are present in ap-modal: ap-name, ap-price, ap-stock, ap-brand, ap-category, ap-sub-category, ap-desc, ap-image, ap-extra-images, ap-sub-features, ap-whats-in-box, ap-spec-tabs (NEW), ap-attrs-brand, ap-attrs-os, ap-attrs-ram, ap-attrs-cpu, ap-attrs-speed, ap-attrs-storage, ap-clothing-size, ap-extra-attrs, ap-price-summary, ap-protection-summary, ap-warranty-summary, ap-delivery-summary, ap-save. End-to-end create with file input requires a real file payload — couldn't be exercised via Playwright fill, but ap-save remains enabled and the form is well structured.

AdminSystemWallet.jsx — 8 group cards are <button> with cursor:pointer, 'Tap to view transactions →' label, click opens g-txns-modal which fetches /api/admin/finance/groups/{group_id}/transactions and renders g-txns-table. g-txns-close dismisses the modal. Works perfectly aside from the testid name mismatch with the QA spec.
REGRESSION ok: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL → https://network-pay-1.emergent.host, /api/branding returns 200, Test@gmail.com/Just@4me logs in and lands on /dashboard.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce the Register 422 bug: goto /register; fill name/email/phone/password where email uses a reserved TLD like '.test' (Pydantic rejects: 'special-use or reserved name'); click reg-submit; observe network call returns 422 with body {detail:[{type,loc,msg,...}]}; verify reg-error is empty and a 'An error occurred in the <div> component' warning prints in console. After the fix in Register.jsx (coerce detail to string with the suggested helper), reg-error should display the joined msg field(s). For the happy path use a .com email — it works end-to-end including the ₹118 pay-fee step. Admin wallet group keys are: revenue, liability, gst, platform_fee, expenses, pending_withdrawals, bank, refunds (NOT the spec's operations/partners/wallets/escrow/payouts/adjustments).
rca of the issue: Register.jsx silent-failure on 422 RCA — When the backend returns 422 from /api/auth/register, FastAPI/Pydantic sends body {detail: [{type, loc, msg, input, ctx}, ...]} (an array of objects). The Register.jsx catch block almost certainly does setError(err.response.data.detail) or {String(detail)} → React tries to render the object/array as a text node → throws → caught as an error boundary warning. Fix: in the catch block, normalize detail before setError: const msg = typeof detail==='string' ? detail : Array.isArray(detail) ? detail.map(d=>d?.msg || String(d)).filter(Boolean).join('; ') : (detail?.msg || 'Registration failed. Please try again.'); setError(msg);
